streaming: In a 12-team league, spend only your final two picks on K and DEF — never reach, since replacement-level options sit on waivers all year. This league's 5-pt bonus for 50+ makes (and 4 for 40-49) tilts kicker value toward big legs on good offenses — Aubrey, Little, Fairbairn, Bates, McPherson — and if you miss the top tier, just stream kickers who are home in domes or facing bend-don't-break defenses. For DEF, draft one unit whose Weeks 1-4 slate is soft, then stream weekly against turnover-prone offenses, rookie/backup QBs, and bad offensive lines; with only 12 defenses rostered, a viable streamer is on waivers nearly every week. The sack (1) and INT/fumble (2) scoring rewards pressure-heavy defenses (HOU, DEN, MIN, PIT) over pure points-allowed profiles. Never carry two defenses or kickers through a bye — drop and stream instead, and note the Week 11 DEF logjam (LAR, SEA, NE, GB, CLE, ATL all off).

strategy.overview: Your edge: the room drafts on Yahoo ADP, which assumes 4-pt passing TDs — this league pays 6. Elite QBs score ~15–20% more here than the default board implies, so QBs are marked up on this board (both numbers shown: my rank AND their ADP). Full PPR pushes target hogs up; 8-of-12 playoffs means draft ceiling over floor.

bands.early: Slots 1–3: You open with a Tier-1 anchor (Gibbs/Bijan/Chase tier). The wait to the R2/3 turn is long — at picks 24–25, Lamar (ADP 38) or the best Tier-3 RB/WR falling to you is the move; don't chase a run you can't catch. Your board wraps around fast after that: plan pairs of picks, not single ones.
bands.mid: Slots 4–9: Balanced lane. Josh Allen (ADP ~20) can land at your R2 pick — take him there; the room won't. Otherwise, two of Tier 2–3 then the Burrow/Daniels/Hurts window in R4–5 while everyone else waits a round longer than they should.
bands.late: Slots 10–12: Back-to-back turn picks. Grab two Tier-2 anchors at 10–15, and Allen at the 13–16 turn is a perfectly fine pick in THIS scoring. Your R3/4 picks (34–39) catch the Lamar/Maye window; use the long waits to plan two picks ahead.

rounds.advice: Best available Tier 1–2, RB/WR only. Gibbs, Bijan, Chase, Puka, JSN class — take the player, not the position.
Elite-QB window opens: Allen (ADP 20) is worth it here in 6-pt TD scoring. Otherwise leave R2 with two anchor RB/WRs.
Lamar goes here on this board (ADP 38 — the room waits). Bowers/McBride if you want the TE edge; else keep hammering RB/WR.
Maye/Burrow value zone — ~QB4 production at a R4/5 price. Fill RB2/WR2 if QB is done; Jeanty ankle discount lives here too.
Last call for the top-QB tier (Daniels/Hurts). McConkey/Egbuka/Waddle types make great WR3s. Don't leave R5 without 2 RB + 2 WR-ish.
RB depth run: Tuten/Henderson/Price won starting jobs. TE second wave (LaPorta/Kraft) if you passed earlier.
Upside WRs — Odunze, Jameson (boom-bust, see flags). Dak/Caleb/Herbert here if you somehow still need a QB — still profits at 6-pt.
Lloyd (confirmed GB starter while Jacobs is out — ADP 111, ranked 78 here) is the prize if he lasts. Warren/Stevenson/Pollard stabilize your flex.
One-QB league, 6 bench spots: do NOT draft a QB2 unless Stafford/Purdy-tier value falls. Take Sutton/MHJ/Pittman value instead.
Value sweep: Godwin (TB WR1 now), Brooks (healthy, splitting CAR work), Kelce discount if you need TE. Check the VALUE badges.
Handcuff your RB1 (Corum for Kyren, Mike Washington for Jeanty, Kaelon Black for CMC — see Handcuffs sheet) or grab a rookie with a job (Lemon, Price).
Kyler (MIN, rush floor, 6-pt TDs) is the best late QB dart if you want insurance. Otherwise: Worthy, Reed, Shaheed upside.
Last skill pick: swing big — Coker, McMillan (TB), Boutte, Likely. A safe backup here wins you nothing in an 8-team playoff league.
Kicker, and only now. Big legs get 5 pts from 50+: Aubrey, Fairbairn, Dicker, Little, Bates — whoever's left.
Defense: best of HOU/DEN/LAR/SEA/MIN still on the board, or the best Weeks 1–4 schedule. Avoid GB (Parsons out 4 games). Stream all season.
